summary: Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and elsewhere under teachers including Hiroshi Tsuchiya and Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji and Professor at Toyo University.
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010). She became an Assistant Professor at Stanford University in 2017.

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge, Oxford, and earned her PhD at the University of Warwick (~1990–1995), where she later became Emeritus Professor.

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at Harvard under Roger Brown (~1963–1969) and held posts at Brown University and the University of California, Berkeley, where she became a professor in 1971.

Elena Bashir is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1982–1988) and held posts at the University of Chicago, including an editorial board position around 2002.
Elena Beccarini-Crescenzi was an Indology scholar who studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini at the University of Florence, completing her studies by 1915.
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian History under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome until 1971, later serving there as an Associate Professor from 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed her Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Tübingen (~2007–2010). She held posts at Tübingen, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and became an Assistant Professor at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned doctorates in Paris under Charles Malamoud and his habilitation at Hamburg. He taught at Vienna and held the Indology chair at Leipzig University (2004–2021).

Elijah George Halhed Impey (1818–1868) was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist who served in the Bombay Medical Service, as Surgeon-Major in the Bombay Army (~1840–1868), and as Postmaster-General in the Bombay Presidency (1856–1868).

Elijah Sacvan Ary (born 1972) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and earned a PhD at Harvard (~2001–2007) supervised by Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Elimar Benda (1890–1976) worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a Dr.iur. at the University of Jena (1913) and held library positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (1921–1922), University of Freiburg (1926–1936), and Heidelberg University (1936–1940).

Elimar Max Grube (1851–1891) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Rudolf von Roth, earning his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (1874–1875) under Albrecht Weber.

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia (1956–1960). He held posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006), also editing Philosophy East and West.

Elisa Freschi (born 1977) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied under Raffaele Torella, held posts at Sapienza University, the University of Vienna, and IKGA, and became an Associate Professor at the University of Toronto around 2020.

Elisa Ganser is an Indology scholar who worked as a project collaborator at the University of Zurich (2018) and is attested as a lecturer at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Elisabeth Kreyenborg (born 1897) was an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. under Richard Schmidt at the University of Münster in 1930. She later served as a librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft from 1943 to 1950.
